chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When a man is angered with his wife and does not approach her, without an oath, for four months, and she seeks enforcement against him, then either he returns (to her) or he divorces her. So if he leaves her from other than anger or an oath, he is not considered a mu'll (one who has taken an oath of abstention).

key_terms.مُؤْلٍ: One who has taken the oath of abstention (Ila)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between separation due to anger and the legal state of Ila (solemn oath of abstention) in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between mere separation due to anger and the specific legal status of 'ila' (solemn oath of abstention), which requires a formal oath to trigger the four-month waiting period. It establishes that without an oath, the husband is not considered a 'mu'll', thereby limiting the wife's right to petition for enforcement or divorce under the specific rules of iila. This ruling underscores the precision Shia fiqh applies to marital contracts, ensuring that emotional estrangement does not automatically invoke the stricter penalties associated with a sworn vow.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the man is angered over his wife, so he does not go near her from without an oath for four months, so he would be disciplined over it. So either he meets (reconciles) or he divorces. So if he neglects her from other than anger, or an oath, so it is not a solemn oath’.
en.sarwar: Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Khalaf ibn Hammad in a marfu‘ manner who has said the following: “About the case of a man’s 7/a’ (swearing), abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘He either expiates or divorces or is beheaded.’”
